employers.name: University of South Alabama / USA Health
employers.note: Higher education and academic healthcare; cited as Mobile County's largest employer. Headcount deliberately omitted — published figures ranged from 3,800 to 7,200 and none could be confirmed against a primary source.

institutions: University of South Alabama — public research university in Mobile; 14,285 students enrolled in fall 2025, a third straight year of enrollment growth.
USA Health — the university's academic health system, operating University Hospital, Children's & Women's Hospital and the Mitchell Cancer Institute.
Spring Hill College — founded 1830; the oldest Catholic college in the Southeast and Alabama's oldest institution of higher learning.
Alabama Port Authority / Port of Mobile — the state's deepwater seaport, which the authority credits with supporting one in seven jobs statewide.
highlights: Africatown — the north-Mobile community founded in 1866 by survivors of the Clotilda, the last known U.S. slave ship. The Africatown Heritage House at 2465 Winbush Street opened July 2023 and houses 'Clotilda: The Exhibition'.
USS ALABAMA Battleship Memorial Park on Battleship Parkway — the WWII battleship USS Alabama, the submarine USS Drum, an aircraft pavilion and armor displays.
Bellingrath Gardens and Home — a 65-acre public garden and house museum on the Fowl River about 20 miles south of Mobile, open to the public since 1932.
Mobile's Mardi Gras — the Gulf Coast's founding Carnival tradition, with the first observance recorded in Mobile in 1699 and the first American-style parade in 1831.
